label: Proton, human brain in vivo
reference: Tetramethylsilane at 0 ppm; in practice the in-vivo scale is set by placing the NAA methyl singlet at 2.01 ppm, and tissue water then falls near 4.7 ppm
note: Heights are peak heights in a short-TE 3T spectrum rather than concentrations, so singlets such as NAA and total creatine stand tall while equally abundant coupled spins such as glutamate are split into low multiplets, and the suppressed water line at 4.7 ppm is some four orders of magnitude larger than anything shown here.

peaks.name: tCr CH2
peaks.full: Total creatine, methylene resonance of creatine plus phosphocreatine
peaks.note: CH2 singlet; creatine 3.913, phosphocreatine 3.930. Close enough to water that water suppression can attenuate it, so it is a poor concentration reference.

peaks.name: mI
peaks.note: The quantified feature is the overlapped H1/H3 (3.52) and H4/H6 (3.61) multiplets, centre about 3.56. Further mI signals at 4.05 (H2) and 3.27 (H5).

peaks.name: Glc
peaks.note: Centre of the ring-proton cluster, range about 3.2 to 3.9 for both anomers. The cleaner alpha anomeric H1 sits at 5.23, downfield of water.

peaks.name: Tau
peaks.note: H1, the CH2 next to the sulfonate; the second taurine CH2 (H2, next to the amine) is at 3.25. Both overlap glucose and myo-inositol.

peaks.name: sI
peaks.note: Singlet from six equivalent CH protons, quoted between 3.34 and 3.35. Low and variable in normal brain, roughly 0.2 to 0.5 mM.

peaks.name: tCho
peaks.full: Total choline (glycerophosphocholine, phosphocholine and free choline)
peaks.note: Trimethylamine N(CH3)3 singlet, nine equivalent protons: glycerophosphocholine 3.212, phosphocholine 3.208, free choline 3.185.

peaks.name: tCr CH3
peaks.full: Total creatine, N-methyl resonance of creatine plus phosphocreatine
peaks.note: N-CH3 singlet; creatine 3.027, phosphocreatine 3.029. The usual internal concentration reference in clinical work.

peaks.name: GABA
peaks.note: H4, the CH2 next to the amine, and the peak recovered by MEGA-PRESS with the editing pulse at 1.9 ppm. Other GABA triplets at 2.28 (H2) and 1.89 (H3).

peaks.name: GSH
peaks.note: Cysteine beta-CH2, the edited peak; the editing pulse is applied to the cysteine alpha-CH at 4.56 ppm.

peaks.name: Asp
peaks.note: Beta-CH2 protons at 2.68 and 2.80, alpha-CH at 3.89. Badly overlapped by the NAA aspartyl multiplets at 2.49 and 2.67.

peaks.name: Gln
peaks.note: H4 (gamma-CH2) multiplet, about 2.43 to 2.46, the most usable glutamine feature at 3T; alpha-CH at 3.75.

peaks.name: Glu
peaks.note: H4 (gamma-CH2) multiplet, about 2.34 to 2.35. Beta-CH2 at 2.04 to 2.12 lies under NAA; alpha-CH at 3.74. Glu and Gln are often reported together as Glx.

peaks.name: MM20
peaks.note: Broad protein methylene and methine envelope, about 2.0 to 2.1, sitting under NAA and glutamate. Prominent at short TE and larger with age.

peaks.name: NAAG
peaks.note: Acetyl CH3 singlet, only 0.03 ppm downfield of NAA, so the two are usually reported together as tNAA.

peaks.name: NAA
peaks.note: Acetyl CH3 singlet, the tallest metabolite peak in normal brain. Its aspartyl protons appear at 2.49, 2.67 and 4.38.

peaks.name: MM17
peaks.note: Broad resonance near 1.7, tentatively assigned to lysine, arginine and leucine side chains; increases from about age 30 to 40.

peaks.name: Ala
peaks.note: CH3 doublet, J about 7.2 Hz, centred at 1.47; alpha-CH at 3.78. A marker in meningioma and abscess.

peaks.name: Lac
peaks.note: CH3 doublet, J about 6.9 Hz, centred at 1.31 with lines near 1.29 and 1.34; CH quartet at 4.10. Inverts at TE near 135 to 144 ms.

peaks.name: Lip13
peaks.note: Bulk fatty acyl (CH2)n plus macromolecules MM12 and MM14, spanning about 1.2 to 1.4. Large in necrosis and tumour, and from subcutaneous fat contamination.

peaks.name: Lip09
peaks.full: Lipid methyl plus macromolecule MM09 resonance
peaks.note: Fatty acyl CH3 at 0.89 together with the MM09 protein methyl envelope near 0.91; present in normal brain at short TE.
